source: Hmm! I merely choose what I say carefully. We only have so much influence to spend, after all.
Do you not do the same, my lady?
But... you know things that haven't happened yet.
You knew about my father dying. You warned me, in so many words.
When you've seen as much as I have, you learn to guess how plots will unfold.
Don't be coy with me. I've earned more information than that, if you have it.
My darling girl, we've already had this conversation, and I've told you what you needed to know.
Let the world be your schoolbook, the ebb and flow of life your teacher!
...And come back to me when you have something truly juicy.
I could share the secret, if you like. You should see some of my newest material! In this humble playwright's opinion, it has a rare novel quality, I think.
Is that an invitation?
I'm afraid our time here runs short. If only you had asked me earlier...
Meet me in the gallery after my performance has concluded, and we'll talk.
You know, not every performance I give is here in the castle. Sometimes, on my way in or out, I do a little extra show. You know. For the children.
You'll come see me, won't you? I feel as though we've grown quite close, these last few days. How many 'days' has it been now? Hrm!
This is my magnum opus! My true life's work! And as you know—vita brevis.
When exactly is this unmissable performance?
Early Thursday morning. Be there if you can.
Does Peter Quince's behavior seem unusual to you?
You did just warn me about him.
And now that I've spoken with my father, I can see why.
It sounds like we are in grave danger from him.
That's why he has to be stopped. This cannot continue.
And given everything that happened afterwards, I have to wonder whether I'm going mad, or you are.
I find myself doubting that something so strange can be true, but Elsinore has been rather a strange place, lately.
I'll speak to my father's spirit about it as soon as I'm able.
Strange? How?
He seems to have an uncanny knowledge of everything that happens in this castle.
Everything that could happen in this castle.
'Could' happen?
As if he's some sort of... fortune teller? You don't truly believe this, do you?
What if he is?
I'd have to wonder whether I was going mad, or you were.
(Right. He hasn't heard of Quince's arrival just yet.)
I've learned he's coming to Elsinore Castle soon to perform. Your mother requested his presence.
Well, that's the best news I've received in months.
Quince always was an odd man. But I never found him odd in an off-putting sort of way.
Does Peter Quince seem at all odd to you?
(Right. She hasn't heard of Quince's arrival just yet.)
He's a traveling performer. Supposedly he's well known in the area, though I'd never met him until recently.
Oh. That one. Yes, I've seen his work. You want to know if he's odd?
Ophelia, we live in a walled castle at the edge of Denmark. All foreigners are 'odd.'
I meant—beside that.
...He always seems to know where to find me, I suppose. Even when I'm not expecting to be found.
He... sought you out?
Yes, when I was running errands in town.
He offered me some peculiar advice. I-it was—well, no. It's nothing.
...He edited your story.
Ah. Never mind.
Always mumbling, you.
He's well known as a sort of... rabble-rouser, I think. He always performs alone.
I rarely trust men who travel alone. They're often up to nothing good.
What do you know of Peter Quince, the Playmaster?
Ah. Him.
The... details are indescribably hazy. It is hard to remember.
But I recall he was kind to me. Kinder than I deserved, considering I was not able to help him.
Of course. Now I now he was just using me for his own ends.
We must stop him, Ophelia. There are no limits to what that man will do.
Help him with what, exactly?
...It was a pressing request of his—something I could not... find...
My memories drift away like fog. Retrieve my final writings from your father. Perhaps then we can make sense of this nothingness.
To help him find the Book of Fates... the token which created this sad situation.
I was never able to find it, of course... but even knowing gave me purpose.
The will to try again indefinitely. The will to return, even now.
Father, I found a note from Laertes on your desk about his lute.
Aha! Yes, that old thing. He's certain the prince's gone and stolen it. But—well...
Frankly, now that your brother's abandoned his costly trip to Paris, he can sort out these petty squabbles himself.
I don't believe Hamlet would've taken it. You know how those two can be. How they've always been.
I never thought two boys raised like brothers could hate one another more.
If I were to track it down and bring it back to Laertes, perhaps that tension would be resolved.
One tension of many, yes.
I'm certain Hamlet or Bernardo will know where it's gone off to, even if they don't know where it is now.
Little to resolve now, with Hamlet's passing. The poor lad.
I would have thought Bernardo to be an excellent voice in mediating this. The poor lad. May he rest in peace.
I found a note from my brother accusing Hamlet of having stolen his lute. Do you know anything about it?
A... stolen lute? From his room? Hrm...
Oh. Oh. I see. Yes, I think I... know precisely what he means.
Have you spoken with Hamlet about this yet?
I have. He wants to meet with you to find it.
Excellent. I'll find him anon.
I haven't, no.
You ought to. For once, his hands are clean of this.
You mean Laertes was right?
Certainly, but... I may have been the culprit. Tell Hamlet to meet me. I'll discuss it with him then.
Unfortunately, things are too hectic at the moment for me to look into Laertes' petty theft cases.
Perhaps the next time there's a... lull, Ophelia? Things are tense in Elsinore.
I found a note from my brother accusing you of having stolen his lute. Do you know anything about it?
You've got to be joking, surely. Yes?
Firstly, that lute hasn't been used in years. Why is he looking for it now? And secondly, I never laid a hand on the damn thing. I can't even play.
Does Bernardo know about this? I'm confident the lute is with him.
I spoke to Bernardo. He asked me to speak to you in turn, so the two of you could meet.
I'll find him and get to the bottom of this.
Not yet, no.
Well, tell him I want to see him at once. Go on, then.
Ophelia, leave me be. Things are stirring in Elsinore, and my priorities are elsewhere. I care little what Laertes thinks right now.
Can't you find me when things are peaceful once more?
My Lord, I know for certain Prince Hamlet will survive his trip to England. I know, also, that this is opposite of your desire.
I-indeed, just this morning, I received word that he's quite alive. In the hands of pirates, no less.
If you... if you're sympathetic to my thoughts and actions...
If you knew of my intentions, why did you not tell me sooner?
If you knew of my plan, why did you not tell me sooner?
W-well, no matter. He's on the ocean now. I can't do anything. May his ship sink all the swifter.
Why on earth would I desire my nephew's death? A trip to England will be just the thing he needs.
You and I both know that isn't true. You want Hamlet dead.
How could you know about this?
Your secret's safe, my lord. For now, that is.
Know, then, that I have ordered Rosencrantz and Guildenstern to deliver a letter to the Crown of England.
And within that letter is writ my nephew's death warrant.
I have faith in those two to bear my letter truly. Even so...
A-as far as I know, you are the only one who knows my true intentions.
If you wish to avail yourself to a King, and so earn my personal favor, perhaps you can join Hamlet on his journey.
And in doing so, ensure his demise.
The ship sails at ten in the morning. Go with him. Ensure he does not return to Denmark, and you will be justly rewarded.
Why on earth would I desire my nephew's death?
Because I suspect he's been rather a thorn in your side as of late.
That's neither here nor there. My nephew is very much alive and well.
And though things have been difficult as of late, I have hope to rectify the situation.
(I see. He hasn't hatched his plan yet.)
Regardless, my lord. If the situation changes, may we discuss it further?
Hamlet—you ought to be wary. Your uncle desires your death at sea.
He means to have you sent away and quietly executed upon arrival. But he will be unsuccessful in this.
...I am, of course, unsurprised.
I suspected something like that was his intention from the moment we boarded this ship.
There's nothing to be done now but watch and wait. I can trust no one but you, Ophelia.
After everything that happened last night...
I had heard there was a plan forming to have me sent to England.
Ophelia, I swear to you it was a mistake. I never meant to harm your father.
But now, I can no more refuse Claudius sending me away than I can bring your father to life again.
Ophelia, I swear to you it was a mistake. I never meant to threaten your father.
But now, I can no more refuse Claudius sending me away than I can undo the attempt I made on your father's life.
The alternative is to face legal punishment here, in Elsinore.
This is functional exile, and it is one I go to willingly.
Nevertheless, I hear your warning, and I shall watch carefully for any sign of this plot.
Death at sea?
I'm not certain I understand what you mean.
(Ah, right. Claudius hasn't asked Hamlet to go to England...)
Guilda, I came to warn you. You and Rosie are both going to be killed.
K-killed?! But how?
When you're both sent to accompany Hamlet to England, the ship's going to be beseiged by pirates, and—
Oh, I love this game. Are we telling tall tales? How fun!
No. I'm telling the truth. I wanted to let you know while there was still time.
I'm not dead now... but I might die. Is that what you're saying?
Yes. Yes, that's it exactly.
Well, they can't kill me if they think I'm already dead. This plan is infallible!
This is all a little much, Ophelia. I think I'll need a few hours to figure out what it means.
